function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that:

| Feature | Details |
|---------|---------|
| **Operating System** | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (focal) |
| **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX A6000 (A6000‑PCIe) |
| **Machine type** | `n1-standard‑8` (8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM) – you can change this to suit your workload |
| **Zone** | `us-central1-a` (replace with a zone that supports A6000 GPUs) |
| **Project** | `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` (replace with your actual project ID) |

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * The **Compute Engine API** and **Cloud GPUs API** must be enabled in your project.  
> * You must have the **gcloud CLI** installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  
> * The zone you choose must support the A6000 GPU. Check availability with:  
>   ```bash
>   gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="name=A6000" --zones=us-central1-a
>   ```

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI Command

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --subnet=default \
  --network-tier=PREMIUM \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --provisioning-model=STANDARD \
  --service-account=YOUR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --image-family=focal \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
  --boot-disk-device-name=rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=./startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--project` | Your GCP project ID |
| `--zone` | Zone that supports A6000 GPUs |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--subnet` | VPC subnet (default is fine for most cases) |
| `--network-tier` | Premium network tier |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Keep the instance running during maintenance |
| `--provisioning-model` | Standard provisioning |
| `--service-account` | Service account with required scopes |
| `--scopes` | Full cloud platform access |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk |
| `--boot-disk-type` | Balanced persistent disk |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional startup script (e.g., install CUDA drivers) |
| `--tags` | Allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic (optional) |

> 📌 **Tip** – If you need more than one GPU, change `count=1` to the desired number (max 8 per instance).

---

## 2️⃣  REST API Call (JSON)

If you prefer to use the REST API directly (e.g., from a CI/CD pipeline), here’s a sample request body you can POST to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances
```

### Request Body (JSON)

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/focal",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "YOUR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y cuda-drivers"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### How to Send the Request

You can use `curl`, Postman, or any HTTP client library. Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

> 🔑 **Authentication** – The `Authorization` header must contain a valid OAuth 2.0 access token. The `gcloud auth print-access-token` command is a quick way to obtain one.

---

## 3️⃣  Optional: Startup Script (install CUDA drivers)

If you want the instance to automatically install CUDA drivers on boot, create a file named `startup.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Update package lists
sudo apt-get update

# Install NVIDIA CUDA drivers
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535

# Reboot to apply driver changes (optional)
# sudo reboot
```

Then reference it in the gcloud command or the REST JSON as shown above.

---

## 4️⃣  Verify Instance Creation

After the command completes, you can verify the instance:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=us-central1-a
```

Look for the `accelerators` section to confirm the GPU attachment:

```yaml
accelerators:
- acceleratorCount: 1
  acceleratorType: zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000
```

---

## 5️⃣  Common Troubleshooting

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Zone doesn’t support A6000** | Run `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="name=A6000"` to find a supported zone. |
| **GPU quota exceeded** | Request a GPU quota increase in the GCP console under IAM & Admin → Quotas. |
| **Instance fails to start** | Check serial port logs: `gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=us-central1-a`. |
| **Driver not loaded** | SSH into the instance and run `nvidia-smi` to verify GPU status. |

---

### TL;DR

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --image-family=focal \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1
```

That’s it! You now have a fully‑functional Compute Engine instance with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. Happy GPU computing! 🚀
